analysis.title: Global Economics Wrap-Up: November 6, 2026
key_insights: DM fiscal health is near its weakest outside major crises, and fiscal rules have done little to stop the deterioration because governments have increasingly suspended or loosened them over the past decade.
Market-driven fiscal consolidations have historically been larger as a share of GDP than discretionary or rules-based ones. They have also hit GDP harder than discretionary ones.

The debt-stabilizing gap (primary balance versus the level that holds debt/GDP stable) has predicted consolidation well. When it exceeded 4pp of GDP, as it does now in France, the US and the UK, a consolidation followed within three years almost half the time.

GS country economists do not forecast meaningful DM fiscal consolidation in 2027 because the recent rise in global yields is not yet large enough to prompt a significant reassessment. Country forecasts imply a roughly neutral 2027 fiscal impulse: expansion in Japan and Germany, consolidation in the UK, a flat impulse in the US. Growth risks are skewed to the downside from potentially larger consolidations.

France is the most likely consolidation candidate given its large debt-stabilizing gap and sharp rise in bond yields. The GS base case is still that the 2027 deficit exceeds the 5.0% target before declining in 2028.
The RBA raised its cash rate 25bp to 4.85% on a 6-3 vote, in line with GS and consensus. GS expects an extended hold before a gradual easing cycle starts in Q4 2027.

The BoE raised Bank Rate 25bp to 4% on an 8-1 vote, with Mann dissenting for 50bp. The split was more hawkish than expected, and communication pointed more strongly to another hike. Bailey said another hike was likely absent a Middle East resolution but pushed back against a prolonged sequence of hikes. GS keeps its February hike forecast, sees a December hike as possible if energy pressures intensify, and says its forecast remains notably below market pricing.

The ECB held rates in October as expected. The Council debated hiking but chose to wait. GS maintains its December hike forecast and sees a March hike as possible if energy prices keep rising, though it sees a significant hurdle to faster hikes.

GS cut its euro area growth outlook on higher energy prices and tighter financial conditions. Q4 GDP tracking is 0.1%qoq excluding Ireland, Q1 and Q2 2027 forecasts are cut to 0.1%qoq and 0.2%qoq, H2 growth is still expected to average 0.3%qoq, and 2027 Q4/Q4 growth is 0.9%.

GS raised its euro area inflation forecasts. Core now peaks at 2.9%yoy in Q2 2027 and headline peaks at 4.2%yoy in 2027Q2, reflecting higher energy forecasts and AI-related demand, with second-round effects limited.

The Riksbank unanimously raised its policy rate 25bp to 2.0%, in line with expectations. It kept balanced communication, saw inflation risks to the upside and growth risks as two-sided, and GS maintains two further quarterly hikes to 2.5% in 2027.
Norges Bank held at 4.5% as expected and reiterated that keeping the policy rate elevated for a time will likely be necessary. GS expects it to stay on hold, with normalisation cuts from Q4 2027.

The October US jobs report showed nonfarm payrolls +165k and the unemployment rate down 0.1pp to 4.1%. Gains were led by healthcare (+55k) and professional and business services (+70k). September was revised up 31k to 60k and August up 53k to 186k, lifting the three-month average to 137k from 51k before the report.
The unemployment rate fell as employment rose 463k and the labor force rose 421k. Participation rose 0.1pp to 61.9%.

Democrats won both the House and Senate in the midterms by much larger margins than expected. GS expects them to use fiscal deadlines to try to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs and reverse last year's spending cuts.

GS expects Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan to impose conditional data center moratoria pending new legislation. That legislation could end certain tax breaks, tighten environmental, water and electricity rules, and make local moratoria easier. GS expects the issue to fade and any moratoria to be short-lived because data centers rank low among voter priorities.

The global composite PMI fell 1.1pt to 53.2 in October, with manufacturing down 0.4pt to 52.6 and services down 1.3pt to 53.2. Canada's manufacturing new export orders fell 2.8pt to 44.6 on renewed US trade tensions. Global manufacturing input prices rose 1.1pt to 62.2 and output prices rose 0.5pt to 55.2.

The PBOC moved its policy rate anchor from the 7-day to the overnight reverse repo rate, set at 1.25%, and raised the FX deposit reserve requirement ratio 2pp to 6%. GS reads this as discomfort with the pace of RMB appreciation over the past two months.

The BOJ held at 1.25% as expected, and GS now expects the next hike in December 2026. Malaysia held at 2.75% (GS still sees a 25bp hike to 3% in Q1) and Colombia held at 12.25%. Egypt hiked 100bp to 20% against a consensus hold, and Ukraine hiked 50bp in a hawkish surprise.

GS's new China Macro Survey points to stable growth over six months with downside risks. Investors are cautious on consumption and inflation and expect only modest fiscal easing. Beijing CIO tour speakers expect a constrained policy backdrop into 2027, resilient but slowing exports, and a 2027 growth target unlikely to be notably below 4.5%.

October manufacturing PMIs weakened in China (official and unofficial), north Asia and LATAM, but were stronger in ASEAN and rose in CEEMEA. China's official PMIs have shown a pattern of weakness in the first month of the quarter over the past two years.

tension_points.bull_case: GS country teams do not forecast meaningful DM consolidation in 2027, because the recent rise in global yields is not yet large enough to force a reassessment. The implied 2027 fiscal impulse is roughly neutral, with expansion in Japan and Germany offsetting consolidation in the UK and a flat US.
tension_points.bear_case: DM fiscal health is near its weakest outside major crises and rules have not held. France, the US and the UK all have a debt-stabilizing gap above 4pp of GDP, after which a consolidation followed within three years almost half the time. Market-driven consolidations are the largest and hit GDP hardest, so growth risks are skewed to the downside.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further sharp rise in bond yields, especially in France, that forces a larger consolidation than GS's base case, which has the 2027 French deficit above the 5.0% target.
